title: tune NCCL overlap scheduling for tensor-parallel multi-GPU workloads
author: Avery Chen
description: Motivation: tensor-parallel workloads suffered from suboptimal overlap between NCCL collectives and local compute in certain model shapes and sequence length distributions. This PR improves scheduling and stream assignment for NCCL collectives, reduces unnecessary CUDA synchronizations, and adjusts KV-cache placement for better locality. The goal is to increase throughput and reduce tail latency without changing public APIs. Summary of changes: 1) Introduce dedicated comm CUDA streams per NCCL communicator and a more deterministic stream affinity policy to avoid interference with compute streams. 2) Implement non-blocking collective launching with explicit CUDA event-based dependencies instead of stream synchronization. 3) Add a lightweight NCCL op scheduler that groups small collectives and delays low-priority all-reduces to improve packing and reduce kernel launch overhead. 4) Move KV-cache shards to the same GPU local memory allocator when possible to reduce cross-device memory traffic during KV cache lookups. 5) Small kernel launches and kernel fusion hints to reduce launch overhead for short token generations. 6) Continuous-batching tuning: adaptive batch delay adjusted to favor packing of small requests under high concurrency. Performance: on internal TP-4 runs with LLaMA-variant 70B test suite we observed ~14-18% throughput improvement at p50 token/sec and 22-27% reduction in p99 latency under mixed prompt lengths. Patch also removes a pathological CUDADeviceSynchronize present in prior tensor-parallel path. See linked benchmarks and flamegraphs. Checklist: - [x] Unit tests for scheduler heuristics - [x] Integration tests for TP multi-GPU runs - [x] Benchmark scripts and automated compare - [x] Docs update for runtime configuration knobs - [x] Performance signoff from perf team Related: ENG-2491 (tensor-parallel perf investigation), ENG-2513 (KV-cache locality study). Notes: this is runtime-only and non-breaking; default behavior is unchanged unless the new runtime knobs are enabled in runtime config.

review_comments: Morgan Lee (reviewer): Could you explain the reasoning for choosing a dedicated comm stream per communicator vs per-device? The per-comm approach may create many streams once we scale to >16 communicators.

Avery Chen (author): Per-comm simplifies matching of NCCL communicators to logical model shards and avoids cross-comm interference. We limit stream creation by reusing streams for communicators with identical device sets; added comment and tests to validate reuse.
Ravi Patel (reviewer): There's a flakiness observed on CI GPU-2 with the non-blocking collects — trace attached. Can we add a fallback to the previous sync path if an environment variable is set?

Avery Chen (author): Added environment fallback REDWOOD_NCCL_LEGACY_SYNC=1 and a unit test that exercises fallback. Also annotated known CI kernel driver issue and added retry logic for event polling.
Sofia Alvarez (perf): Please add numbers for short-sequence workloads; we saw regressions previously. Also confirm p99 with batching off.

Avery Chen (author): Added short-seq microbenchmarks (benchmarks/tp_nccl_overlap/short_seq.sh) showing neutral to small positive wins (1-5%); when batching is disabled we still retain 6-8% throughput uplift due to reduced sync points.
merge_details: Merged by Morgan Lee using squash merge. Merge commit message: 'tune NCCL overlap scheduling for TP: dedicated comm streams, non-blocking collectives, KV-cache locality, continuous batching tweaks (ENG-2491, ENG-2513)'.
release_notes: runtime: Improve tensor-parallel multi-GPU performance by tuning NCCL scheduling and reducing sync points. Adds runtime knobs for comm stream affinity and adaptive continuous-batching delays. Expected throughput improvements for TP workloads; opt-in via runtime config.
notes_for_ops: Ops: new runtime knobs (comm_stream_policy, nccl_scheduler_enabled, continuous_batching.delay_ms) default to conservative values. To enable aggressive packing set nccl_scheduler_enabled=true and comm_stream_policy=per_communicator. Monitor /metrics/runtime/nccl_collective_latency and /metrics/runtime/kv_cache_hits for regressions.
additional_context: This PR builds on earlier PRs that targeted NCCL collectives and TP overlap (see pr-23789, pr-22678). The scheduler heuristics are intentionally small and parameterized so we can A/B with runtime flags. We plan a follow-up to add automatic knob autotuning under Redwood Optimize.
changelog_entry: perf: tune NCCL overlap scheduling and KV-cache locality for tensor-parallel; p99 latency reductions and throughput gains in mixed workloads
